paper_metadata.title: Homogenization effects by Co additions to high temperature and low stress creep performance of a 4th-generation Ni-based single crystal superalloys

evidence.quote: The effects of Co and inhomogeneity between dendrite core (DC) and interdendritic region (ID) on creep performance at 1100 °C and 137 MPa in a 4th generation Ni-SXs were systematically investigated.

The γ phase early crystalizes to form DC, where contains more refractory elements (such as Re and W), while ID solidifies later and precipitates γ / γ ′ eutectics.

In high magnification SEM images in Fig. 2(b, c, e, f, g, h) , the DC region of the three alloys is precipitated by fine γ ′ phase precipitate, while the coarsened γ / γ ′ microstructure was observed at ID.
When the boundaries of the DC are highly distinguishable, amounts of eutectic phases are noticed in the ID region (see the inset in Fig. 2 (a)).

once the highly heterogeneous γ / γ ′ microstructures at the DC and ID region are transformed into regular and uniform microstructures composed of cubical γ ′ particles and narrow γ matrix channels, the difference between DC and ID is indistinguishable.

Another microstructure feature is TCP phases, which are precipitated at 70 h creep in 5.9Co alloy, nor the other alloys, indicating that the addition of Co is conducive to inhibiting the precipitation of TCP phases.
TCP phases are precipitated at DC of all alloys after long-time uphill diffusion of solution strengthening elements
The as-cast morphology displays the typical dendritic microstructures in the three alloys, as shown by the low-magnification images in Fig. 2 (a), (d), and (g).

In primary creep, as shown in Fig. 10 , most of γ ′ phase has been coalesced and rafted with N- type (normal to stress axis) in 5.9Co alloy, while relatively regular γ / γ ′ microstructures remain in the other two alloys.

At secondary creep, most of dislocations still move in γ matrix and are restricted by γ / γ ′ interface, and a few of them shear in γ ′ phase to form superdislocations (see the green arrow), which destroy the integrity and continuity of the dislocation network
The large-size cracks (about 40 μ m, the yellow shape) appear in all Ni-SXs at ID, which are distributed in rows perpendicular to the stress axis.
However, the cracks at DC are relatively small (about 10 μ m, the orange circle).
